Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the new passenger terminal building at Kushok
Bakula Rimboche Airport, Leh, built at a cost of Rs. 640 crore, sped over 23,800 square
metres. The modern terminal is designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually. Prime
Minister will also dedicate to the nation the 298-kilometre-long Niyamopadum Darsha
road constructed by border roads organization, connecting Yemu in Leh with Darcha in Himachal
Pradesh through the remote Zanskar valley. As part of effort to strengthen energy security
and harness Ladakh's renewable energy potential, Prime Minister will inaugurate the nine-megawatt
HANU small hydroelectric project and 66 KV double-circuit Da HANU Khalsa transmission
line.
Prime Minister will inaugurate India's first petrograph conservation park at Sindhugat
Leh. Ladakh is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites. For Akashwani News, this is
Punsukh Wangmok from Leh Ladakh.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with the Indian contingent that participated
in the Asian Games 2026 in New Delhi this evening. The Prime Minister will also address
the gathering on the occasion.
India finished fourth in the medal Delhi at the Asian Games held in Aichi Nagoya,
Japan, winning 85 medals including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. This marked
India's second consecutive finish among the top five nations at the Asian Games, reflecting
the country's growing competitiveness across a diverse range of sporting disciplines. India
also recorded several notable achievements at the Games, including historic performances
in recurve archery, gold medals for both the men's and women's hockey teams in the same
edition, and median medals in soft tennis and mixed martial arts. Other significant
achievements included India's first-ever gold medal in the Women's Trap event, a silver medal in
weightlifting at the Asian Games after a gap of 28 years, and a silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling,
ending a 64-year wait for an Indian finalist in the discipline.
Nethika Gupta, Agarswani News, Delhi
Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved a productivity
productivity-linked bonus PLB equivalent to 78 days wages for over 11,40,000 railway employees.
Briefing media after the cabinet meeting, information and broadcasting minister Ashwani
Vaishnav said government is allocated over 2,009 crore rupees for this payout.
The cabinet today approved a productivity-linked bonus equivalent to 78 days wages for around
11,470 railway employees. The bonus is a Diwali gift for all railway employees who work tirelessly
day and night to ensure the smooth functioning of the Indian railways. The total financial
outlet for the bonus is approximately Rs.2,009 crore. The maximum bonus amount payable per
eligible employee is Rs.17,951 for the 78 days. It covers Group C railway personnel,
including track maintainers, locomotives, train managers' guards, station masters'
supervisors, technicians, pointsmen, and ministerial staff. Cabinet Committee of
Economic Affairs CCEA has approved strategic restructuring of IDBI Bank.
The government has constituted a committee to examine issues raised by
sugarcane farmers and recommend appropriate measures for addressing
their concerns. Former member of Nitiayok, Professor Ramesh Chand, will chair
the committee which included Agriculture Commissioner, Joint Secretary Suga, Department of Food and
Public Distribution and Joint Secretary Legal Metrology, Department of Consumer Affairs
as members. The constitution of the committee follows the decisions taken during a meeting
of representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra with the
Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare and the Union Minister of Consumer
affairs, food and public distribution. More from a correspondent.
The committee will examine the demand for an increase in remunerative returns to sugarcane
farmers taking into account cultivation costs and other relevant factors. It will also
examine the demand for revision of the X-mil minimum selling price of sugar in the context
of sugar production costs, market realizations and the financial viability of sugar mills.
Other key areas of examination will include existing mechanisms for testing and reporting
sugar recovery and prevailing sugarcane weightment practices at sugar mills.
The committee will also examine prevailing practices relating to deductions from the
weight of mechanically harvested sugarcane and assess the extent of actual losses,
if any, arising from mechanized harvesting.
It will evaluate the financial impact of the present practices on the cane price
payable to farmers and may consider any other related matters deemed necessary.
With Anand Kumar, Rishu Jaiswal, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare will celebrate the national-level celebration
of Mahila Kisan Divas 2026 in New Delhi today to recognize the women's contribution
to Indian agriculture.
The Minister of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare said that women being an integral part
of India's agricultural system play several pivotal roles from sowing, transplanting
in harvesting to livestock management seed conservation and natural resource management,
with the traditional knowledge and biodiversity, conservation entrepreneurial initiatives and
adoption of sustainable agricultural practices, women's strength in brutal livelihoods and
enhanced agricultural resilience. This is Akash Vani giving you the news.

President Drupati Murmur will inaugurate the National Sahara's livelihoods mailer
2026 at Punnami Ghat in Vijaywara today. For the first time the national level
fair has been held outside the Delhi National Capital Region. We have a report.
The National Saras Mila 2026 being held in Vijaywada provides a platform for rural women
from self-help groups across the country to showcase their products, reach wider markets
and strengthen their livelihoods. Organized by the Union Ministry of Rural Development,
in association with the Andhra Pradesh government, the fair brings together around 1500 women
entrepreneurs and artisans. More than 650 stalls display traditional
hand-loom products, handicrafts, organic goods and household items.
The Mela also features regional food, live demonstration of traditional crafts and training
in packaging, branding and online marketing.
National Saras Mela highlights the Lakpati Didi initiative, which aims to help rural
women achieve sustainable incomes and financial independence.
Allumerli, Akashvani News, Vijawada.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva, Sadesh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushashan, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a vixit Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming
lives.
Today, in a special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated
into action through institutions like RERA, which are working towards transparency and
consumer rights in the real estate sector.
Parliament enacted the Real Estate Regulation and Development Act in 2016, paving the
way for establishment of real estate regulatory authorities, RERAs, in states.
Under the Act, real estate projects must be registered with the regulatory authority
before developers can advertise, market or sell properties subject to the applicable
provisions of the law.
RERA provides a regulatory mechanism for addressing disputes between developers and home buyers
ensuring greater transparency and accountability in the real estate sector.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that RERA has played a significant role in strengthening
understanding trust between homebuyers and developers.
Anil Tiwari, a resident of Gautam Buddha Nagar, said that Raira has enhanced transparency
between developers and buyers. He added that regulatory framework has encouraged builders
to commence projects on time and enabled home buyers to receive possession of their homes
as scheduled.
RERA has helped improve relations between developers and buyers while providing legal protection
to the rights and interests of property buyers, Sushilchandra Tiwari, Akashwani News, Lucknow.

Around 57,500 Durga Pujas are being organized across West Bengal this year, including more than
3,300 in Kolkata alone. From grand, theme-based pandals to traditional community and household
worship, the celebrations showcase Bengal's rich cultural heritage and artistic creativity.
Thousands of people have already begun visiting pandals,
while crowds are expected to grow further over the coming days.
Police and civic authorities have stepped up security, traffic management, and crowd
control arrangements to ensure safe and smooth celebrations.
Shrondipandash Gupta, Akash Bani News, Kolkata.
